title: Al-Bayyinah: sincere devotion
hookLine: all they were asked was to worship Allah sincerely, pray, and give (98:5)

lines: SOME INSTRUCTIONS FIT ON YOUR HAND.
cards: Some instructions are long. The tax form, the terms and conditions, the washing machine manual. And some are short enough to write on your hand.
Yesterday's surah described people arguing and dividing, even after a clear sign had come. Then, right in the middle, it stops and says, in effect: here's all you were ever asked. One verse.
A short list, with the words naught else in front of it.

teach.b: Verse five of Surah al-Bayyinah, in Pickthall's translation: And they are ordered naught else than to serve Allah, keeping religion pure for Him, as men by nature upright, and to establish worship and to pay the poor-due.
Naught else. Nothing more than this. Look at the pieces.
First, keeping religion pure for Him.
The Arabic is mukhlisin, from the same root as al-Ikhlas, which we met a few weeks ago: sincerity, purity, nothing mixed in. Worship done for Allah, not for an audience or a reputation.

Second, as men by nature upright: hunafa'. A hanif is someone who turns away from idols toward the one God, and the Qur'an's great example is Ibrahim. It suggests something straight, not bent by pressure.
Third and fourth, prayer and giving, salah and zakah, named side by side here as in other verses: one toward Allah, one toward people. Sincere, upright, praying, giving.
The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ put the first piece at the head of everything.
The very first hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari says: actions are only by intentions, and each person gets only what they intended.
Two people can do the same prayer, the same donation, side by side, one for Allah and the other to be seen. From the outside, identical. Inside, not the same act at all.
A short list, and the first item is the one nobody else can check.

how: Muslims speak of niyyah, intention, before acts of worship, and many recall the hadith 'actions are only by intentions'; Islamic teaching encourages hiding some good deeds so they stay sincere.

o: a secret teaching kept for a few chosen believers
a long code of rules for every part of daily life
the clear proof, a surah whose core is sincere worship

games.q: what's inside the verse — tap the pairs.
p: upright, turned to the one God

s: 98:5 gives a long list of rules
naught else: sincere worship, uprightness, prayer, giving.
mukhlisin shares a root with al-Ikhlas
two identical acts always count the same
the hadith says each person gets what they intended.

games.q: two people give the same donation, side by side. one does it for Allah, one to be seen. what does the first hadith of Bukhari say?
o: they're equal; the money is the same
each gets only what they intended
the one who gave publicly gets more
games.why: actions are only by intentions. from the outside identical; inside, not the same act.

practice: Choose one act to do purely for Allah, or, if that's not your language, purely for the good of it: something nobody will see or thank you for, like paying for a stranger's coffee without saying so, or cleaning something that isn't yours.
Then check your intention honestly, and if any part of it is for how it looks, make it quieter until it isn't.

wordCard.voice: Al-Bayyinah. The clear proof, and the surah whose center says: all that was asked is sincere, upright worship, prayer and giving. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: sincere ones, making worship pure; the root of al-Ikhlas.

carryVoice: Your line: sincere and upright. Naught else was asked. Day one hundred seventy-nine, done.

sources.q: And they are ordered naught else than to serve Allah, keeping religion pure for Him, as men by nature upright, and to establish worship and to pay the poor-due.
